answer: A graph-distance attestation quota resists sybils. Only endorsements crossing the attestation vine count: a newcomer needs peers at least three hops away, proven by walking the edge list. Each peer signs two endorsements per epoch, drawn from a cipher-seeded sample, so the mapping cannot be farmed ahead. Splitting into n aliases earns nothing shared, since internal signatures sit inside the cluster and are discarded. Endorser slots are scarce saffron: supply is capped, so an attacker must bid n times for one fixed pool, and price per alias climbs with each added identity.
